message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: publish nuget

on: 
  push:
    tags:
    - '*'

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: windows-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v1

    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj', '**/*.sln', '**/packages.lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-

    - name: Set tag to version
      run: dnx DotNetCampus.TagToVersion -t ${{ github.ref }}

    - name: Build with dotnet
      run: |
        dotnet build --configuration Release
        dotnet pack --configuration Release --no-build

    - name: Push generated package to GitHub registry
      run: |
        dotnet nuget push .\\artifacts\\package\\release\\*.nupkg -s https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json -k ${{ secrets.NugetKey }}
        dotnet nuget push .\\artifacts\\package\\release\\*.nupkg -s https://nuget.pkg.github.com/${{ github.repository_owner }} --api-key ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs dotnet build and dotnet pack on every tag push, restoring NuGet dependencies on each run. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions, 2024, section 4.2.1, Table 4) supports caching dependency downloads with reported modest VM time reduction (free: 6%, paid: 3.4%). Preconditions are met: dependency fetching is repeated across runs, and cache inputs can include project/lock files and runner environment. No contraindications apply: NuGet packages are trusted dependency downloads rather than mutable build outputs, and no equivalent cache exists. The change adds a single cache step before the build, preserving all existing build, pack, and push steps and required coverage without adding privileges, secrets, publishing operations, or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
